function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service" in PowerShell. Or use "docker-machine start default" if using Docker Machine. But the user likely wants to start Docker Desktop. So we can provide a command: "net start com.docker.service". Or "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service". Or "docker start" is wrong. So we should explain that docker start starts containers, not the Docker engine. Provide correct command.

We have a tool to execute commands. We can call functions.cmd_controller_execute with command "net start com.docker.service". That will start the Docker service. Let's do that.
